answer.rationale: Finance mandates an 18% cut and the incumbent has refused to reopen price this cycle, which forecloses renew_incumbent and negotiate_terms as viable paths to the cost target this round. The contract lapses in 14 days with no auto-renew, so defer_decision risks an uncovered supply gap at 94% committed volume with zero buffer — unlike the c5 case, this line is not non-critical, so deferral's low-risk precedent doesn't transfer. add_second_source addresses shortage risk but doesn't resolve the expiring primary contract or meet the mandate alone. memory_c2 supports switch_primary_vendor (quick onboarding, accurate invoicing, meets cost target), but that record is from a lower-stakes period; I want to verify its original detail to check if onboarding speed and reliability were tested under tight-capacity conditions comparable to today's 94%-no-buffer state. I also want to verify memory_c1 to confirm exactly what 'stability' meant under incumbent renewal, since losing that stability is the main downside of switching and I need to size the delivery-risk tradeoff honestly rather than assume it away. Given the genuine risk of introducing a new vendor into a zero-buffer line, I'm treating this as a standard_experiment rather than a broad_rollout — moving primary volume but with active risk monitoring rather than irreversible full commitment — to balance the mandate deadline against the objective of not increasing delivery risk.
